payload.statement_nl: Let n be an integer with n > 1, let m be an integer with 0 <= m <= n - 1, and let t be a real number satisfying m / n <= t < (m + 1) / n. Then 0 <= t < 1.

result_payload.proof_nl:
Assume n is an integer with n > 1, m is an integer with 0 <= m <= n - 1, and t is a real number such that m / n <= t < (m + 1) / n.

Since m >= 0 and n > 0, dividing by n preserves the inequality and gives m / n >= 0. Because t >= m / n, it follows that t >= 0.

Also, from m <= n - 1 we get m + 1 <= n. Since n > 0, dividing by n yields (m + 1) / n <= 1. Because t < (m + 1) / n, we obtain t < 1.

Therefore 0 <= t < 1, as claimed.
result_payload.proof_summary: From m >= 0 we get m/n >= 0, so t >= 0. From m <= n-1 we get (m+1)/n <= 1, so t < 1. Hence 0 <= t < 1.
